abstract: The adoption of social companion AI (SCAI) is often framed in terms of the positive features it offers users, including its nonjudgemental nature, agreeableness, and availability. Here, we argue the appeal of these features primarily arises from the difficulties inherent in human sociality. SCAI reduces what we term relational complexity, or the demands and risks inherent in human relationships. Drawing insights from studies of human cognition, communication, and human-computer interaction, we identify six distinct sites of relational complexity that we posit are integral to understanding SCAI adoption. These include: (i) relationship formation and dissolution; (ii) achieving mutual understanding; (iii) interpersonal motives and strategic uncertainty; (iv) social partner evaluation and self-presentation; (v) social embeddedness and information flow; and (vi) reciprocity and relationship maintenance. By attenuating relational complexity, SCAI offers users some of the experiences associated with companionship while reducing the demands intrinsic to obtaining such experiences from another person. However, the lower interpersonal risk and diminished cognitive load that attracts users to SCAI may contribute to myriad negative impacts, including relationship displacement, social demotivation, social deskilling, and risks to privacy. The concept of relational complexity thus provides a framework for studying both the appeal of artificial companionship and its implications for human wellbeing.

ur.tldr: 社交陪伴AI的吸引力常被归因于其非评判、顺从与随时可用等正面特征。本文提出"关系复杂性"框架，识别出关系形成与终结、互相理解、动机与策略不确定性、伙伴评估与自我呈现、社会嵌入与信息流动、互惠与关系维护六类复杂性来源，解释用户为何转向AI陪伴，同时指出关系替代、社交去动机化、社交去技能化与隐私风险等负面后果。

title: Relational Complexity: Making Sense of Social Companion AI Use
title_zh: 关系复杂性：理解社交陪伴AI的使用
